data.long_meaning: Madhavi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Madhava', which means 'God of wealth'. In Hindu mythology, Madhavi is also associated with the goddess Lakshmi, the deity of wealth and prosperity. This name is a symbol of beauty, abundance, and good fortune. The name Madhavi carries the meaning “Goddess of wealth, beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Madhavi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth, beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit, Goddess of wealth and mother of Lord Krishna
vedic_reference.note: Madhavi is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Madhava', which refers to Lord Krishna himself. In Hindu mythology, Krishna is often depicted as the god of wealth and abundance. The name Madhavi is thus a tribute to both the divine mother and the divine son.

historical_references.reference: According to the Mahabharata, Madhavi was a celebrated courtesan of ancient India who is said to have enchanted the great sage Vyasa with her beauty and charm. She is mentioned in the Anushasana Parva (Book of Instructions for a Ruler) as the embodiment of 'love in its purest form'.

Madhavi is also the name of a goddess in Hindu mythology, specifically the goddess of love, Lakshmi, who is often depicted with her consort Vishnu as Madhava. The name Madhavi is derived from Madhava, which means 'enchanter' or 'all-attracting' in Sanskrit. The mythology surrounding Madhavi and Vishnu represents the divine union of love and wisdom.
